currentContext.expansion: Zydus undertook strategic investments to expand formulations manufacturing capacity for the US and international markets: enhancing Oral Solid Dosage (OSD) capacity at its Ahmedabad SEZ Unit II and Baddi facilities to support growing US demand, and capacity-expansion initiatives at its Moraiya and Goa facilities to address international formulation markets. It is establishing a new, highly automated 'Lights Out Factory' OSD facility at Ahmedabad SEZ Unit III, integrating robotics, Industry 4.0 technologies and AI-enabled analytics for a near-zero-touch manufacturing environment, and separately commissioned commercial operations at a new Unit III monoclonal-antibody (mAb) drug-substance biologics facility during FY2025-26. The Company entered the global biologics CDMO business by acquiring two US-based biologics manufacturing facilities from Agenus Inc. in California (operating as Zylidac Bio), establishing a US manufacturing presence. In vaccines, it expanded bacterial and recombinant vaccine manufacturing facilities to address rising global demand and commenced supply of the Measles-Rubella vaccine under India's Universal Immunisation Programme. In the API business, it expanded capacity for key molecules to support growing formulations demand and invested in processing capabilities, production resilience, validation infrastructure and IT systems. In Consumer Wellness, it continued capacity expansions and technology-led manufacturing upgrades, including commissioning of new manufacturing capacity. On the MedTech front, it identified three priority segments -- Orthopaedics, Nephrology and Cardiology -- completing the acquisition of Amplitude Surgical (a leading European orthopaedics player), which includes a manufacturing facility in Valence, France capable of producing hip and knee prostheses, and is separately establishing a new manufacturing plant for high-end dialysers in Nephrology. It also made a capital investment of Rs 383 million on energy-conservation equipment during the year, and incurred expenditure including capital expenditure of Rs 13,838 million on research and development on a standalone basis.

risks.risk: Regulatory change and non-compliance across global drug regulators
risks.note: The AR's Key Risks table states the pharmaceutical industry faces risks from evolving regulatory requirements, and that any non-compliance may lead to regulatory actions, increased costs and reputational impact affecting operations. Mitigation rests on independent audits and stringent cGMP compliance checks to maintain audit readiness against global quality standards.

risks.risk: Generic price erosion, new-entrant competition and government price control
risks.note: Flagged in the Key Risks table as intense competition in the generics segment leading to pricing pressure and erosion of market share, with entry of new players in existing products and markets intensifying competition and government-imposed price controls in certain geographies impacting margins and profitability. The stated response is volume expansion, new launches, and moving up the value chain to complex products with higher entry barriers.

risks.risk: Product quality failure causing supply suspension and blocked new approvals
risks.note: BRSR material-issue #11 (Product Quality and Safety, negative financial implication) is unusually explicit: failure to maintain quality standards and comply with regulations leads to regulatory actions which result in suspension of supply of products and cessation of new product approvals from the concerned sites. That is the site-level revenue chokepoint for a US-facing generics maker; mitigation is a quality management system, a Quality Risk Assessment Program covering data integrity, and automation for all-time audit readiness.

risks.risk: Legal, IP and tax litigation exposure
risks.note: A named Key Risk covering failure to protect intellectual property rights alongside regulatory actions related to pricing and quality. Patent challenges and IP outcomes gate exclusivity and first-to-file economics in the US generics business, and tax litigation is carried as a standing exposure. (The description and mitigation column for this row are cut off mid-sentence in the routed AR text, so only the risk heading and opening clause are verbatim.)

risks.risk: Geopolitical and trade disruption in export markets
risks.note: Key Risks table cites exposure to political and economic uncertainties including policy shifts, geopolitical tensions and conflict situations that can disrupt operations and create volatility in business performance across affected regions. Notably, mitigation is financial rather than operational — monitoring exposure to high-risk regions and securing receivables through letters of credit or advance payments, which points to credit risk on emerging-market export receivables.

risks.risk: Supply chain partner concentration and business continuity
risks.note: BRSR material-issue #10 (negative implication) states supply chain partners spread across various geographies are responsible for on-time delivery of input materials, products, services and capital goods critical to operations, and that any threat to the sustainability of those partners' operations could potentially disrupt the Company's operations. The mitigation of creating a multiple supplier base for critical products implies single-source dependency exists where that has not yet been done.

risks.risk: R&D data security and retention of the scientific talent pool
risks.note: BRSR material-issue #8 (negative implication) identifies access control, archival and retrieval of R&D data as absolutely critical since any leakage can lead to substantial loss of future opportunities, and names tenure of the scientific pool and knowledge transfer as critical specifically when working on complex dosage forms and technologies. For a company pivoting to complex/specialty products, pipeline value is tied to individuals; the stated comfort is that a majority of senior leadership at technology centres has been with Zydus for over a decade.

BRSR material-issue #9 (negative implication) notes regulatory authorities have a zero-tolerance policy against unethical marketing and promotion activities under stringent regulations, and that non-compliance can bring penal action and loss of goodwill. Relevant given the Company's multi-market branded and prescription presence and its interactions with healthcare professionals.

one-line thesis: Zydus delivered record Q4FY26 profitability (33.7% EBITDA margin) driven by mix shift to specialty and forex, while strategically pivoting toward high-margin oncology via the proposed Assertio acquisition and launching first-in-class biosimilars. Guidance for FY27 remains robust with >24% margins despite heavy R&D and commercial spend on Saroglitazar, signaling a structural re-rating from generic volume player to specialty innovator.

margins & cost dynamics: Q4 margin expansion driven by product mix, operating leverage, forex; FY27 margin guidance >24% absorbs ₹70cr Saro commercial spend, Revlimid/Mirabegron competition, and ~8% R&D intensity.
capex / expansion: FY27 Capex guidance: ₹1,500cr focused on MedTech (dialyzer membrane), biologics facilities, and specialty portfolio expansion; Depreciation elevated due to capitalized Mirabegron license amortization.
capital allocation: Prioritizing bolt-on specialty acquisitions (orphan/rare disease); Comfortable with ~1.0x Net Debt/EBITDA post-Acquisitions (Assertio/Buyback); Working capital days remain best-in-class despite absolute increase from M&A.
risks & watch-items: Assertio deal closure/integration risk; Saroglitazar US FDA approval timeline uncertainty; Revlimid/Mirabegron price erosion faster than expected; MedTech platform scaling slower than 3-4 year horizon.

non-obvious takeaways: Mirabegron depreciation charge is a finite accounting distortion (ends Sep-2027) masking true cash profitability; Semaglutide co-marketing with Lupin/Torrent was a strategic share-of-voice play that secured #2 market position rapidly rather than a margin-compromise; Assertio deal viewed as synergy-positive (commercial leverage) rather than cost-additive.

themes.title: Pharma US complex-generics & specialty exports
themes.need: US complex generics, Para-IV FTFs and the GLP-1/semaglutide wave still drive export pharma, but Q1FY27 delivered one hard setback and one deliberate trough. DRREDDY held an out-of-cycle call disclosing a semaglutide injectable API scale-up validation failure - an out-of-spec impurity in finished product - halting supply through roughly September and re-cutting FY27 volumes to 6-7 million pens (Q3-Q4) from an earlier ~12mn first-year target, which re-times India's largest semaglutide launch and opens a share window for rivals. CIPLA let EBITDA margin fall to 16.7%, below the pre-Revlimid level, because launch opex is committed ahead of revenue plus ~1-2% of revenue in war-related input cost - yet reaffirmed BOTH an FY27 18.5-20% margin and a $1bn US exit run-rate off a $162m Q1, making this a trough by design with unusually large operating leverage if the launches land. The GLP-1 opportunity is bifurcating: CIPLA's Yurpeak (tirzepatide, Eli Lilly collaboration) did INR 80cr and is already the #2 anti-obesity brand behind Mounjaro while Cipla deliberately sits out the crowded semaglutide-generic price war. NATCOPHARM remains in a gRevlimid post-cliff base year; LUPIN/ALKEM/ZYDUSLIFE/LAURUSLABS carry cleaner momentum; SENORES/MARKSANS on US generics; DIVISLAB on GLP-1 peptides (55% CDMO mix).
themes.driver: DRREDDY's semaglutide supply restart (guided ~September) and whether the 6-7mn-pen re-cut holds; CIPLA's four US launches landing against the reaffirmed 18.5-20% FY27 margin; FTF launches and USFDA clearances; DIVISLAB Kakinada Unit 3 from FY27.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global economy remained resilient through 2025 despite trade tensions and tariff disruption; global growth is expected to moderate slightly to 2.6% in 2026 before recovering to 2.7% in 2027 as trade normalises and uncertainty fades.
- India remained one of the fastest-growing major economies, supported by strong services/industrial performance and resilient domestic consumption, with the RBI easing monetary policy; external factors such as geopolitical developments and crude-oil volatility are flagged as near-term inflationary risks, though expected to remain manageable.
- The global pharmaceutical industry (~USD1.67 trillion in 2025, +~10% YoY) continues to be led by Oncology, Immunology and Diabetes, with Obesity/weight-management emerging as one of the fastest-growing therapy segments; the US remains the largest and a growing share of global pharma sales (53% in 2025, up from 52%).
- A wave of patent expirations is opening opportunities for generics and biosimilars — around 15 blockbuster drugs valued at about USD112 billion globally are expected to face patent expiry, including semaglutide's India patent expiry in March 2026, which is expected to improve access to Type-2 diabetes/obesity treatment via generic entrants.
- The Indian pharmaceutical market grew 9.9% in FY2025-26, led by Cardiac, Gastro-Intestinal, Anti-Infectives and Anti-Diabetic therapy areas, with India's pharmaceutical exports rising steadily and the sector continuing to be described as the 'Pharmacy of the World' on the back of manufacturing scale and cost efficiency.
- Global demand for biologics, biosimilars, vaccines and targeted therapies remains strong, driven by rising chronic-disease prevalence, increasing healthcare expenditure, and advances in biotechnology, precision medicine and AI-driven drug development.
- The global biologics CDMO market is expanding rapidly (from ~USD23.1 billion in 2025 toward ~USD55.1 billion by 2035), with Asia-Pacific emerging as the fastest-growing region on expanding manufacturing capability and cost advantages.
- The global specialty pharmaceuticals market (biologics, orphan drugs, gene therapies, precision medicines) is projected to grow from ~USD311.7 billion (2024) to ~USD519.8 billion by 2035, driven by the rising burden of chronic illness and continued innovation in advanced treatments.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q4 margin expansion driven by product mix, operating leverage, forex; FY27 margin guidance >24% absorbs ₹70cr Saro commercial spend, Revlimid/Mirabegron competition, and ~8% R&D intensity.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing bolt-on specialty acquisitions (orphan/rare disease); Comfortable with ~1.0x Net Debt/EBITDA post-Acquisitions (Assertio/Buyback); Working capital days remain best-in-class despite absolute increase from M&A.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Zydus undertook strategic investments to expand formulations manufacturing capacity for the US and international markets: enhancing Oral Solid Dosage (OSD) capacity at its Ahmedabad SEZ Unit II and Baddi facilities to support growing US demand, and capacity-expansion initiatives at its Moraiya and Goa facilities to address international formulation markets. It is establishing a new, highly automated 'Lights Out Factory' OSD facility at Ahmedabad SEZ Unit III, integrating robotics, Industry 4.0 technologies and AI-enabled analytics for a near-zero-touch manufacturing environment, and separately commissioned commercial operations at a new Unit III monoclonal-antibody (mAb) drug-substance biologics facility during FY2025-26. The Company entered the global biologics CDMO business by acquiring two US-based biologics manufacturing facilities from Agenus Inc. in California (operating as Zylidac Bio), establishing a US manufacturing presence. In vaccines, it expanded bacterial and recombinant vaccine manufacturing facilities to address rising global demand and commenced supply of the Measles-Rubella vaccine under India's Universal Immunisation Programme. In the API business, it expanded capacity for key molecules to support growing formulations demand and invested in processing capabilities, production resilience, validation infrastructure and IT systems. In Consumer Wellness, it continued capacity expansions and technology-led manufacturing upgrades, including commissioning of new manufacturing capacity. On the MedTech front, it identified three priority segments -- Orthopaedics, Nephrology and Cardiology -- completing the acquisition of Amplitude Surgical (a leading European orthopaedics player), which includes a manufacturing facility in Valence, France capable of producing hip and knee prostheses, and is separately establishing a new manufacturing plant for high-end dialysers in Nephrology. It also made a capital investment of Rs 383 million on energy-conservation equipment during the year, and incurred expenditure including capital expenditure of Rs 13,838 million on research and development on a standalone basis.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and aggressive on specialty pivot; Transparent on margin headwinds from R&D/launch costs; Emphasizes 'platform building' over short-term EPS in MedTech/Biologics.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- 3rd largest generic company in the US by prescriptions (IQVIA MAT March 2026 TRx)
- Amongst Top 3 in ~55% of the product families it markets in the US
- Global manufacturing network of 44 facilities spanning small molecules, API, biologics, vaccines, consumer wellness, animal health and medical devices
- R&D scale: 10 R&D Centres and >1,500 R&D scientists supporting a pipeline spanning NCEs, biosimilars, complex generics and vaccines, with R&D spend at ~8.4% of revenue in FY2025-26
- Broad distribution reach across 81 countries via distributors, hospitals, B2B API supply and contract manufacturing/CDMO arrangements
- Diversified portfolio (branded pharma, wellness, MedTech) reduces reliance on any single business line

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Assertio deal closure/integration risk; Saroglitazar US FDA approval timeline uncertainty; Revlimid/Mirabegron price erosion faster than expected; MedTech platform scaling slower than 3-4 year horizon.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Mirabegron depreciation charge is a finite accounting distortion (ends Sep-2027) masking true cash profitability; Semaglutide co-marketing with Lupin/Torrent was a strategic share-of-voice play that secured #2 market position rapidly rather than a margin-compromise; Assertio deal viewed as synergy-positive (commercial leverage) rather than cost-additive.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body: The Company has formulated a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy pursuant to SEBI Listing Regulations regulation 43A, uploaded on the Company's website; the text provided does not elaborate further on payout philosophy, debt-reduction intent or reinvestment priorities beyond confirming the policy's existence and regulatory basis.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Intensifying price competition in GLP-1 and oncology supportive care; high R&D burn rate for new launches. | Sun Pharmaceutical Industries | beneficiary | Med | As the largest domestic peer, Sun benefits from the overall sector re-rating towards specialty complex generics, though Zydus's specific moves in oncology supportive care (Assertio) directly challenge Sun's existing portfolio. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [M&A] Acquisition of Assertio Holdings Inc. completed during the quarter, targeted at the US specialty portfolio.
- [JV] Joint venture agreement signed with Sunshine Healthcare Lanka Limited for a pharmaceutical manufacturing facility in Sri Lanka.
- [NCE pipeline] USFDA granted priority review to the New Drug Application of Saroglitazar Magnesium for the treatment of Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC); regulatory approval received in India to initiate Phase III trials of Desidustat in patients with sickle cell disease.
- [Biotech/Vaccines] Initiated Phase III trials in India for the company's second biosimilar antibody drug conjugate; completed Phase II of a bivalent Typhoid Conjugate vaccine and initiated Phase I of a Chikungunya vaccine in India; the Measles and Rubella (MR) vaccine dossier submitted to WHO has been accepted for review.
- [US exclusivity] Received USFDA approval for Indocyanine Green for Injection with 180-Days CGT exclusivity.
